notes: Read all 205 source lines line by line before editing. The hook has three browser surfaces: (1) the Notification permission gate (permission/requestPermission), (2) the deprecated in-app `new Notification(...)` toast (sendNotification), and (3) the Web Push (VAPID) PushManager subscribe/unsubscribe lifecycle (subscribe/unsubscribe, isSubscribed, currentEndpoint) that registers this browser-device pairing with the server. CONVERSION STRATEGY: runtime feature detection via globalThis casts (NOT a hard stub). This app has a react-native-web target (vite.config.mts / index.web.tsx / the react-native-web dependency) where window.Notification, window.PushManager and navigator.serviceWorker genuinely exist, so on that target the full lifecycle runs 1:1; on bare native (iOS/Android/Windows/macOS Hermes) those globals are undefined so every feature-gated branch falls through to its exact unsupported return — the same shape the web hook itself returns in a browser lacking these APIs. This mirrors the established native precedent of feature-detecting browser globals through globalThis casts (ImportPreviewModal.tsx for atob; GrafanaPanelPage/JsonFormatter/ResponseViewer for navigator.clipboard) and is strictly more faithful than the all-false useNativeWebPush() shim inlined in BrowserPushChannelCard.tsx because it restores real functionality on the web target while preserving the same return shape. The server contract (GET /push/public-key, POST/DELETE /push/subscribe) is reached through the already-ported native ../api/hooks/usePush hooks.

L2 `import { useSubscribePush, useUnsubscribePush, usePushPublicKey } from '@/api/hooks/usePush'` -> `import { usePushPublicKey, useSubscribePush, useUnsubscribePush } from '../api/hooks/usePush'`: the @/ alias is rewritten to the relative path of the already-ported native parity module (apps/native/src/web-parity/api/hooks/usePush.ts), which exports the same three hooks with the same REST contract.

L4 `const isSupported = typeof window !== 'undefined' && 'Notification' in window` -> module-scope `const NotificationGlobal = (globalThis as {Notification?: WebNotificationCtor}).Notification` + `const isSupported = typeof NotificationGlobal !== 'undefined'`. globalThis is `window` on react-native-web (so the detection is equivalent) and `global` on bare native (where Notification is undefined -> isSupported=false). L5-8 `const isPushAPISupported = typeof window !== 'undefined' && 'PushManager' in window && 'serviceWorker' in navigator` -> module-scope `const pushManagerGlobal = (globalThis as {PushManager?: unknown}).PushManager`, `const serviceWorkerContainer = (globalThis as {navigator?: {serviceWorker?: WebServiceWorkerContainer}}).navigator?.serviceWorker`, and `const isPushAPISupported = typeof pushManagerGlobal !== 'undefined' && typeof serviceWorkerContainer !== 'undefined'`. Same feature-detection semantics, native-safe (no direct DOM global references that would fail the no-DOM-lib native tsconfig).

L10-16 the urlBase64ToUint8Array JSDoc and L17-28 the helper body are ported. `const rawData = atob(base64)` -> feature-detected `const decode = (globalThis as {atob?: (input: string) => string}).atob; if (typeof decode !== 'function') throw new Error('atob is unavailable in this environment'); const rawData = decode(base64)` (the ImportPreviewModal.tsx atob precedent). The padding math `'='.repeat((4 - (base64String.length % 4)) % 4)`, the `(base64String + padding).replace(/-/g,'+').replace(/_/g,'/')` url->std base64, the fresh `new ArrayBuffer(rawData.length)` + `new Uint8Array(buf)` allocation, and the `for` charCodeAt copy loop are byte-identical. Return type `Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>` -> `Uint8Array` (assignable to the applicationServerKey type below; avoids the TS5-only generic). The helper is only reached from subscribe() after the PushManager gate, so on bare native the throw is never hit.

Native-safe browser-only behaviour (contract rules 4,5,7): window.Notification / window.PushManager / navigator.serviceWorker / window.focus / atob are all browser-only. Each is feature-detected off globalThis so the hook runs the full web lifecycle on the react-native-web target and degrades to the documented unsupported shape on bare native, surfaced explicitly via pushStatus + WEB_PUSH_UNAVAILABLE_REASON. No DOM-only modules, browser HTML elements, react-i18next, lucide-react, Recharts, Leaflet, or web UI components are imported — only react's useCallback/useEffect/useState and the native parity ../api/hooks/usePush hooks; DOM types are modelled by minimal local interfaces. Gates run from apps/native: npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit); npm run lint -- --quiet; npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles.
